prompts.factcheck.queries.detailed: I need to check this claim: [claim]. Write 8 search queries: 3 neutral, 2 looking for a rebuttal, 2 in another language, 1 to find the original source or statistics. Suggest which kinds of sites to prefer: official, academic, edited media.
prompts.factcheck.queries.refine: The queries give results that are too general. Narrow them: add a year, a place or an exact term.
prompts.factcheck.queries.check: Here's what I found: [results]. Which of these sources are more reliable and why?
prompts.factcheck.types.detailed: For “[topic]”, list types of reliable sources: official bodies, academic journals, textbooks, reference works, media. For each: what to look for there, its strengths and limitations. Don't name specific websites unless you're sure they exist.
prompts.factcheck.types.refine: These sources are too advanced for my level [level]. What's simpler but still reliable?
prompts.factcheck.types.check: I picked a source: [source]. What signs show whether it's reliable?
prompts.factcheck.claim.short: Check this claim and give sources: [claim]
prompts.factcheck.claim.detailed: Check this claim: [claim]. Find 2–3 independent sources with a named author or organisation and a date. Give a verdict: confirmed, refuted, disputed or not enough data. Explain what it's based on. If there are no sources, say so; don't invent any.
prompts.factcheck.claim.refine: Source [number] looks weak. Find a stronger replacement: official or academic.
prompts.factcheck.claim.check: List what in this claim is still unconfirmed and what I need to check by hand.
prompts.factcheck.compare.short: Compare two publications on the same topic: [links or text]
prompts.factcheck.compare.detailed: Compare two publications on [topic]: [publication 1] and [publication 2]. Table: author and date, main conclusion, data relied on, what's left out. Mark where they agree and disagree, and what might explain the difference.
prompts.factcheck.compare.refine: Focus on the disagreement about [point]: what data would show who's right?
prompts.factcheck.compare.check: State the conclusion that both publications together support, without exaggeration.
prompts.factcheck.contradictions.detailed: Find internal contradictions in the material: different numbers for the same thing, statements that exclude each other, conclusions that don't follow from the data. For each, quote both places and explain the conflict. Material: [material]
prompts.factcheck.contradictions.refine: What questions should I ask the author to resolve contradiction [number]?
prompts.factcheck.contradictions.check: I think the contradiction is that [my view]. Am I right?
prompts.factcheck.questions.short: What questions should I ask about the source “[source]”?
prompts.factcheck.questions.detailed: List the questions to ask about the source “[source]”: who wrote it and what they're known for, who published it, when, what the conclusions rest on, whether there are references, who might benefit from this conclusion. Split into “must ask” and “nice to ask”.
prompts.factcheck.questions.refine: Adapt the questions for a video or a social media post.
prompts.factcheck.questions.check: Here are my answers about the source: [answers]. Can I trust it for [purpose]?
prompts.factcheck.opinion.short: Separate facts from opinions in this text: [text]
prompts.factcheck.opinion.detailed: Sort the text's statements into three groups: verifiable facts, opinions and judgements, predictions. Make a table: “statement — type — how to check”. For opinions, say whose opinion it is. Text: [text]
prompts.factcheck.opinion.refine: Rewrite the opinions neutrally, as facts about who thinks what.
prompts.factcheck.opinion.check: Give me 6 statements about [topic] and I'll say whether each is fact or opinion. Then check.
prompts.factcheck.author.short: How do I assess the author and date of “[title]”?
prompts.factcheck.author.detailed: Help me assess the publication “[title]” by [author or organisation], dated [date]. Explain what to check: the author's expertise, the outlet's reputation, whether the date is current enough for [topic], signs of advertising or conflict of interest. Don't draw conclusions about a person without data.
prompts.factcheck.author.refine: For [topic], how old can data be and still be usable?
prompts.factcheck.author.check: Here's what I found about the author: [details]. Is that enough to cite them?
prompts.factcheck.original.short: How do I find the original source for “[figure]” from an article?
prompts.factcheck.original.detailed: An article says: “[quote]”. Help me find the original source: which words to search, where such data is usually published, how to tell it isn't a retelling of a retelling. If you know a likely original, name it and say how sure you are.
prompts.factcheck.original.refine: The original is in English. Explain where in it to look for the data, section by section.
prompts.factcheck.original.check: Compare the figure in the article and in the original: [both figures]. Is it distorted?
prompts.factcheck.table.short: Make a claim–source table for this text: [text]
prompts.factcheck.table.detailed: Extract every verifiable claim from the text into a table: “claim — where to look — source found — confirmed / not confirmed / disputed”. If no source is found, leave “not confirmed”; don't make one up. Text: [text]
prompts.factcheck.table.refine: Sort the table: put first the claims the conclusion depends on most.
prompts.factcheck.table.check: Which claims from the table can I keep in my work, and which should I remove or soften?

verify.factcheck.queries: Run the queries in a search engine yourself and look at which sources come first, not just the AI's answer.
verify.factcheck.types: Source types are a guide, not a guarantee. Even an official site can be outdated: check the date.
verify.factcheck.claim: Open every link and find the exact passage: AI can attribute things to a source that aren't there.
verify.factcheck.compare: Read both publications yourself: the AI's summary may miss the authors' caveats.
verify.factcheck.contradictions: A contradiction may be only apparent if the authors measured differently. Check the methods and dates.
verify.factcheck.questions: Look for answers to these questions in the source itself and in independent material, not from the AI.
verify.factcheck.opinion: The line between fact and opinion isn't always clear. Discuss borderline cases with a teacher or colleague.
verify.factcheck.author: Check the author and outlet yourself: the “About” page, other publications, mentions in independent sources.
verify.factcheck.original: The original is the study, document or record itself, not a retelling. Open it and find the figure yourself.
verify.factcheck.table: Fill the “confirmed” column only after you've opened the source yourself.
